architectural_implications.after: Workflow engine externalizes plan, memory, and pending decision points; agents sleep and are woken by signals.
architectural_implications.before: Agent loop holds state in context and runs until completion.
architectural_implications.consequence: Reliability requirements shift to state persistence, idempotent resumption, and replay — the same problems as distributed workflow systems.
architectural_implications.observation: Durable execution replaces continuous inference as the runtime core for multi-day tasks.

architectural_implications.after: Agent initiates a request with full context to a specific person and blocks on a decision; human responds asynchronously.
architectural_implications.before: Human opens chat, describes task, reviews output.
architectural_implications.consequence: Needs routing/ownership logic, escalation policies, and an audit record of who approved what and when.
architectural_implications.observation: Human-in-the-loop becomes an async approval service rather than a chat front end.

architectural_implications.after: Every email, call, document, meeting note, custodian feed, and market move becomes an event that can create or revise agent work.
architectural_implications.before: Agents act only on explicit prompts.
architectural_implications.consequence: Ingestion, deduplication, and signal-to-plan attribution become critical infrastructure; noisy signals become a correctness risk.
architectural_implications.observation: A signal ingestion layer sits upstream of all agents.

architectural_implications.after: Firm knowledge and client history are structured so agents can retrieve and act on them.
architectural_implications.before: Institutional knowledge lives in people and ad hoc processes.
architectural_implications.consequence: Workflow standardization becomes a prerequisite engineering task, not a documentation chore.
architectural_implications.observation: Operational context must be formalized before agents can use it.

article_ideas.audience: AI engineers, platform architects, and agent runtime builders
article_ideas.thesis: Teams building enterprise agents are optimizing the wrong axis when they treat multi-day work as a longer inference session; stop-start workflows with actors, handoffs, and external waits require durable execution primitives—checkpoints, signal wakeups, and idempotent resume—and architectures without them will fail in production regardless of model quality.

core_insights.generalization: Any agent task that spans multiple days or crosses organizational boundaries should be modeled as a durable, resumable workflow with explicit decision points rather than a long prompt chain.
core_insights.insight: Long-horizon work is distinct from long-running work: it is a stop-start workflow spanning days with many actors, decision points, and handoffs, not continuous token generation. This implies the core engineering problem is durable state and re-entry, not long context or long inference sessions.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Most agent runtimes are optimized for a single continuous loop. If real enterprise work is stop-start over days, the runtime's primary job becomes persisting intent, waiting on external events, and resuming correctly — a workflow/durability problem, not an inference problem.

evidence_quotes.text: Agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.
Instead of humans prompting an LLM chat interface, agents execute 90% of the work and pull humans in only when approval or human execution is required.

core_insights.generalization: For autonomous systems, treat human input as an async, addressable service the agent calls (request + wait + resume), not as the initiating client of the system.
core_insights.insight: The interaction model is inverted: agents do ~90% of the work and prompt humans at specific approval/execution points, rather than humans driving a chat interface. The human becomes a step in the agent's workflow, not the workflow's operator.
core_insights.why_it_matters: This relocates human-in-the-loop from the front-end entry point to an approval/notification primitive inside the orchestrator, which changes how you design UX, permissions, audit trails, and blocking vs non-blocking handoffs.

evidence_quotes.text: Every email, call, document and event, from inside the firm and out.

System state must update dynamically based on unstructured human inputs across multiple communication channels.

core_insights.generalization: Design an ingestion layer that converts all multimodal internal/external events into durable signals that can re-trigger and revise active agent plans, rather than requiring re-prompting.
core_insights.insight: Signals are a first-class primitive: unstructured human activity (a lunch conversation recorded by an advisor into the CRM) is ingested as an event that wakes background agents and mutates the in-flight plan.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It shows how plans stay valid in the real world — the state update channel is the same channel humans already use (email, calls, notes, custodian feeds, market data), so agents must treat organizational exhaust as a control input.

evidence_quotes.text: Harnesses provide tools, guardrails, and persistent memory.
Background agents ingest signals, consult operational context and memory via harnesses, execute tasks in sandboxes, and collaborate with humans when decisions are needed.

core_insights.generalization: Separate the agent's policy/context layer from its execution environment so that tools, memory, and constraints can be versioned and audited without changing where effects occur.
core_insights.insight: Harness and sandbox are separate concerns: the harness holds tools, guardrails, and persistent memory, while execution of side-effecting actions happens in sandboxes.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Splitting policy/context (harness) from execution (sandbox) gives a natural fault boundary for irreversible actions and a place to enforce guardrails independent of the model's reasoning.

core_insights.insight: Removing humans from the critical path is framed as the precondition for new capabilities (proactivity, emergent cross-agent coordination), not merely a latency optimization — compressing days to minutes changes what goals are even expressible.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes latency as a capability boundary: some behaviors (e.g., proactively preparing plans before anyone asks) are computationally infeasible while a human sits in the inner loop.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Aman Singh
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Building and operating long-horizon AI agents that run financial services at Arca
  • Purpose: To share engineering insights and architectural patterns for deploying autonomous long-horizon AI agents in financial services. Aman Singh, Lead AI Engineer at Arca, explains how Arca operates as an AI-native financial services firm where AI agents run the business rather than just assist it. He details the difference between short-running tasks and long-horizon work spanning days, weeks, or months, and outlines the core primitives—signals, operational context, harnesses, and people integration—used to build reliable, scalable agent-driven financial operations.

Topic Map

What is an AI-Native Financial Services Firm

  • Explanation: Arca provides financial services like financial planning, tax planning, asset management, and investment advice using AI agents that execute decisions rather than just acting as copilots.
  • Key claims:
    • Agents run the business, not just assist it.
    • Clients range from tech executives to individuals reaching milestones.
    • AI-native means agents execute decisions that shape business outcomes.
  • Examples:
    • Serving technology executives planning early retirement and families buying homes after reaching their first million dollars.
  • Terminology:
    • AI-native
    • financial services firm
    • long-horizon agents
  • Why it matters: Redefines enterprise software by shifting from SaaS tools to AI-operated businesses.

Long-Horizon Work vs. Long-Running Work

  • Explanation: Financial services tasks involve stop-start workflows spanning multiple days, actors, decision points, and handoffs rather than continuous token generation.
  • Key claims:
    • Work is long-horizon, not long-running.
    • Involves multi-day client goals with stop-start execution.
    • Involves many actors, decision points, and handoffs.
  • Examples:
    • A 10-day tax payment workflow involving statement analysis, trading assets to raise cash, ACH settlement, and client confirmation.
  • Terminology:
    • long-horizon
    • stop-start work
    • decision points
  • Why it matters: Highlights why standard LLM chaining approaches fail for multi-day enterprise workflows.

Primitives for Long-Horizon Work

  • Explanation: To enable agents to handle end-to-end outcomes, Arca provides four key primitives: signals, operational context, a harness, and human collaboration.
  • Key claims:
    • Signals keep agents aware of internal and external events.
    • Operational context gives agents firm knowledge and client history.
    • Harnesses provide tools, guardrails, and persistent memory.
    • People are pulled in at the right moment with necessary context.
  • Examples:
    • Background agents reading inbound emails, calls, documents, meeting notes, and market movements.
  • Terminology:
    • signals
    • operational context
    • harness
    • client memory
  • Why it matters: Provides a robust architectural framework for building multi-day autonomous agent systems.

Emergent Complexity and Proactive Operations

  • Explanation: By taking human bottlenecks out of the critical path and enabling background agents to monitor signals and communicate with each other, Arca shifts from reactive assistance to proactive business execution.
  • Key claims:
    • Removing humans from the critical path compresses timelines from days to minutes.
    • Agents watch the world via signals so humans don't have to babysit workflows.
    • New business goals like proactivity become possible when agents drive tasks.
  • Examples:
    • Agents automatically preparing client tax plans every January before anyone asks.
  • Terminology:
    • emergent complexity
    • proactivity
    • background agents
    • signal routing
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates how AI-native architecture transforms firm productivity and service delivery.

Key Points

Arca is not a SaaS company

  • Explanation: Arca does not sell software to other businesses; Arca is the financial services firm itself running operations using applied AI.
  • Evidence: We're an applied AI company that happens to be running a services business in this industry.
  • Practical implication: Companies building AI-native operations can capture service margins rather than just software subscription revenue.

Signals close context gaps

  • Explanation: Background agents continuously monitor emails, phone calls, documents, meetings, custodian feeds, and market data to keep agents updated.
  • Evidence: Every email, call, document and event, from inside the firm and out.
  • Practical implication: Autonomous agents require real-time ingestion of multi-modal firm data to maintain situational awareness.

Agents prompt people, not people prompt agents

  • Explanation: Instead of humans prompting an LLM chat interface, agents execute 90% of the work and pull humans in only when approval or human execution is required.
  • Evidence: Agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.
  • Practical implication: Inverts the standard co-pilot interaction model into an autonomous workflow model.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Arca Long-Horizon Agent Architecture

  • How it works: Background agents ingest signals, consult operational context and memory via harnesses, execute tasks in sandboxes, and collaborate with humans when decisions are needed.
  • Components:
    • Signals
    • Operational context
    • Harness
    • Client memory
    • Sandbox
  • When to use: For multi-day, multi-step financial or enterprise workflows requiring persistence and human-in-the-loop approvals.

Examples & Case Studies

Client Jane owes $100K in taxes by April 15 and emails Arca for help covering it.

  • Illustrates: Long-horizon work involving tax planning, asset liquidation, trade settlement, ACH transfer, and advisor confirmation.
  • Lesson: Long-horizon agents must manage stop-start workflows across multiple days and different internal roles (advisors, traders, operations).

Jane takes an advisor out to lunch, mentions wanting $20K of her bonus applied to taxes, and the advisor notes it in the CRM.

  • Illustrates: Human work acting as a signal that wakes up background agents to update agent plans.
  • Lesson: System state must update dynamically based on unstructured human inputs across multiple communication channels.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Separate short-running chat tasks from long-horizon multi-day workflows.
    • Design systems to ingest all internal and external signals as background events.
    • Build persistence and memory layers to maintain state across days.
  • Strategic:
    • Shift from SaaS software provider models to AI-native service firms.
    • Invert interaction patterns so agents prompt humans rather than humans prompting chat interfaces.
    • Standardize firm workflows so operational context can be cleanly operationalized by agents.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How do you handle edge cases and hallucinations in multi-day financial asset liquidations?
    • What guardrails are necessary when agents autonomously route tasks between departments?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Arca runs financial planning, tax planning, and asset management primarily through autonomous long-horizon agents. (firm architecture claim)
  • Background agents can successfully monitor signals across emails, calls, and custodians to drive multi-day financial workflows. (technical architecture claim)

Notable Quotes

"Arca is an AI-native financial services firm." "What we mean by AI native is that agents run the business." "Agents prompt people more than people prompt agents."

Compressed Summary

  • Arca is an AI-native financial services firm where agents run the business.
  • Financial work is long-horizon and stop-start, spanning days and multiple roles.
  • Architecture relies on signals, operational context, persistent harnesses, and people integration.
  • Agents continuously monitor the world and prompt humans when approval is needed.
  • Keywords: agents, financial-services, long-horizon, ai-native, automation
  • Core insight: In an AI-native firm, autonomous agents drive multi-day operational workflows by ingesting signals, maintaining long-term memory, and prompting humans only when decisions are required.

  - proactivity
  - background agents
  - signal routing
- **Why it matters**: Demonstrates how AI-native architecture transforms firm productivity and service delivery.
## Key Points
### Arca is not a SaaS company
- **Explanation**: Arca does not sell software to other businesses; Arca is the financial services firm itself running operations using applied AI.
- **Evidence**: We're an applied AI company that happens to be running a services business in this industry.
- **Practical implication**: Companies building AI-native operations can capture service margins rather than just software subscription revenue.
### Signals close context gaps
- **Explanation**: Background agents continuously monitor emails, phone calls, documents, meetings, custodian feeds, and market data to keep agents updated.
- **Evidence**: Every email, call, document and event, from inside the firm and out.
- **Practical implication**: Autonomous agents require real-time ingestion of multi-modal firm data to maintain situational awareness.
### Agents prompt people, not people prompt agents
- **Explanation**: Instead of humans prompting an LLM chat interface, agents execute 90% of the work and pull humans in only when approval or human execution is required.
- **Evidence**: Agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.
- **Practical implication**: Inverts the standard co-pilot interaction model into an autonomous workflow model.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Arca Long-Horizon Agent Architecture
- **How it works**: Background agents ingest signals, consult operational context and memory via harnesses, execute tasks in sandboxes, and collaborate with humans when decisions are needed.
- **Components**:
  - Signals
  - Operational context
  - Harness
  - Client memory
  - Sandbox
- **When to use**: For multi-day, multi-step financial or enterprise workflows requiring persistence and human-in-the-loop approvals.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Client Jane owes $100K in taxes by April 15 and emails Arca for help covering it.
- **Illustrates**: Long-horizon work involving tax planning, asset liquidation, trade settlement, ACH transfer, and advisor confirmation.
- **Lesson**: Long-horizon agents must manage stop-start workflows across multiple days and different internal roles (advisors, traders, operations).
### Jane takes an advisor out to lunch, mentions wanting $20K of her bonus applied to taxes, and the advisor notes it in the CRM.
- **Illustrates**: Human work acting as a signal that wakes up background agents to update agent plans.
- **Lesson**: System state must update dynamically based on unstructured human inputs across multiple communication channels.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Separate short-running chat tasks from long-horizon multi-day workflows.
  - Design systems to ingest all internal and external signals as background events.
  - Build persistence and memory layers to maintain state across days.
- **Strategic**:
  - Shift from SaaS software provider models to AI-native service firms.
  - Invert interaction patterns so agents prompt humans rather than humans prompting chat interfaces.
  - Standardize firm workflows so operational context can be cleanly operationalized by agents.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How do you handle edge cases and hallucinations in multi-day financial asset liquidations?
  - What guardrails are necessary when agents autonomously route tasks between departments?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Arca runs financial planning, tax planning, and asset management primarily through autonomous long-horizon agents. (firm architecture claim)
- Background agents can successfully monitor signals across emails, calls, and custodians to drive multi-day financial workflows. (technical architecture claim)
## Notable Quotes
> "Arca is an AI-native financial services firm."
> "What we mean by AI native is that agents run the business."
> "Agents prompt people more than people prompt agents."
## Compressed Summary
- Arca is an AI-native financial services firm where agents run the business.
- Financial work is long-horizon and stop-start, spanning days and multiple roles.
- Architecture relies on signals, operational context, persistent harnesses, and people integration.
- Agents continuously monitor the world and prompt humans when approval is needed.
- **Keywords**: agents, financial-services, long-horizon, ai-native, automation
- **Core insight**: In an AI-native firm, autonomous agents drive multi-day operational workflows by ingesting signals, maintaining long-term memory, and prompting humans only when decisions are required.
